text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.5% today, a modest gain in what has been a strong two-week run of nearly 13%. The move reflects the volatile backdrop for oil prices: crude is trading at $101.91 domestically and $126.55 globally, with geopolitical tensions in the Middle East — particularly Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and shipping routes — creating upside pressure on energy stocks even as traders briefly hoped for diplomatic progress today.

Over the past week, the stock has swung with oil market swings, jumping nearly $5 on October 16th when Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure drove crude higher, then holding most of those gains through today. As a major oil and gas producer, ConocoPhillips benefits directly when global crude prices rise — and the $24-a-barrel gap between world and US oil prices reflects supply concerns that support the broader energy sector.
